title: Cotognata Siciliana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A dense, jewel-toned quince paste, cooked down slowly with sugar until thick enough to slice, its deep amber color and intense fruit flavor a beloved Sicilian autumn tradition.
longDesc: Cotognata requires patience above all, the quince pulp simmered and stirred for a long stretch until it reduces to a thick paste that will set firm enough to slice cleanly once cooled, traditionally poured into decorative molds.
ingredients: 600 g (3 cups) granulated sugar, approximately (equal weight to the cooked pulp)
steps: Cut the quinces into chunks (no need to peel or core first) and simmer in water to cover until very soft, about 30-40 minutes.
Pass the cooked quince through a food mill or fine sieve to remove skins and seeds, yielding a smooth pulp.
Weigh the pulp and combine with an equal weight of sugar in a clean pot.
Add the lemon juice and cook over low heat, stirring very frequently, for 45-60 minutes, until the mixture becomes very thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Pour the thick paste into shallow molds or a dish lined with parchment, smoothing the top.
Let set at room temperature for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight, until firm enough to slice.
Cut into pieces and serve, or store for later use.
chefTips: Stir frequently during the long cooking stage to prevent scorching, especially as the mixture thickens.
The paste is ready when a spoon dragged through it leaves a clear trail that does not immediately fill back in.
This keeps remarkably well, making it an excellent make-ahead treat or homemade gift.
commonMistakes: Not cooking the paste long enough, resulting in a mixture too soft to slice once cooled.
Stirring infrequently, which risks scorching the thick mixture on the bottom of the pot.
Rushing the setting time, cutting into it before it has properly firmed up.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for several weeks, or refrigerate for longer.
healthBenefits: Quince provides fiber and vitamin C, though this is primarily a sugar-based confection.
culturalNote: Cotognata is a beloved Sicilian autumn tradition, its intense quince flavor and jewel-like color making it a favorite paired with aged cheese or enjoyed on its own.
